LESSON: MELODY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENTS
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.6: Melody
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Melody, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENTS.

Key inquiry question: How are melodies varied?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Melody together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner keenly listens or observes simple familiar tunes availed to them and sings or

sign sings along with others.

• Creativity and Imagination: The learner collaboratively sings or sign sings simple songs and makes varied body movements

to represent melodic phrases.

• Critical thinking and Problem solving: The learner uses basic shapes to identify melodic phrases which are similar and

23

different.

• Learning to Learn: The learner applies knowledge and skills acquired in lower grades to sing or sign sing simple songs and

make varied body movements to represent melodic phrases.

Values:
• Respect: The learner performs before peers and accepts feedback,

• Unity: The learner in groups sings or sign sings simple songs and makes varied body movements to represent melodic

phrases in the song.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Peace and Education: The learner sings or sign sings familiar songs that convey peace messages.

Link to other learning areas:

Language Activities: The learner sings or sign sings simple familiar songs in different languages to identify melodic phrases.

Suggested learning resources.

Hearing aids, whistles, flags for signals.
